subject: Canary traffic graduation & operator playbook for VPC switchover
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, carlos.mendez@acme.com
Cc: elena.ruiz@broadcloud.com
Date: 2026-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Canary traffic graduation & operator playbook for VPC switchover

All — putting the canary graduation window and operator runbook into one place so Ops at Acme has a single source of truth for the switchover tomorrow. Key asks up front:
- Acme to confirm they can shift 1% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% steady states on our traffic mirror API by 11:30 PT.
- BroadCloud to keep an eye on packet loss and BGP flap alerts (Elena, thanks for standing by).
- Redwood on-call to validate KV cache hit-rate and prefix priming during step increases.

Attached: operator_playbook_v1.2.pdf (playbook), canary-traffic-matrix-20260823.csv (traffic plan), kv-warmup-steps.txt (priming steps).

Highlights from the playbook (short):
1) Pre-window: warm KV cache by running the directed-seed job 30m before traffic cut. Expect ~75% hit rate before step 1.
2) Step ramp: 1% for 10m with SLA checks, then 10% for 20m, 25% for 40m, 50% for 30m. Each step has an explicit abort criteria (error rate >1.5x baseline OR p95 latency >200ms).
3) Eviction sanity: monitor KVM evictions during step increases; if eviction rate exceeds 2/minute, pause and run priming pass.
4) Rollforward vs rollback decision matrix included in the playbook (simple majority of operators + product lead).

Carlos/Acme: Can you confirm your traffic steering runbook matches the attached matrix? If we get a quick "green" I will kick off priming at 10:30 PT.

Thanks — Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@acme.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@broadcloud.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-23T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Canary traffic graduation & operator playbook for VPC switchover

Maya — thanks for the consolidated playbook. Acme DevOps confirms we can do the 1/10/25/50 progression and our routing team has the TTLs adjusted. A few quick items:
- We will start the mirror at 11:30 PT (1%) and hold for 15 minutes instead of 10 to gather additional traffic shape data.
- We will surface an incident channel (PagerDuty + Slack #acme-go-live) and an on-call infra lead (me).
- We have one ask: if KV cache priming fails to get to 70% hit-rate during the 1% hold we want a recommended priming loop (you suggested a 30m directed-seed). Can we shorten to a 2x directed-seed at 10m and re-measure?

I'll be online during the window.

— Carlos
Carlos Mendez
Head of DevOps, Acme Payments
carlos.mendez@acme.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@acme.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T10:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Canary traffic graduation & operator playbook for VPC switchover

Agree with Carlos on the 15m hold for the 1% step — gives us better baseline variance. On priming: OK to run a 2x quick directed-seed at +10m if hit-rate <70%, but we need to treat it as a stop-gap. If that doesn't bring hit-rate to target we should trigger the priming & sticky-session workstream before stepping to 10%.

Operational checks I'll own during the window:
- p50/p95 token service latency (p95 target <200ms)
- Redis/KV eviction counters and heap pressure
- Queue depth for async inference workers (alert at >500 backlog)

I've uploaded a short checklist to the shared doc and added inline operator commands (see link).

-Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Production Engineering, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-23T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Canary traffic graduation & operator playbook for VPC switchover

+1 from my side. I'll be on the bridge and will run the rollout commands per the playbook. Quick note: I added an extra health-check probe to the canary route that checks token-service readiness and kv-hits; it should reduce noisy step failures.

— Connor
Connor O'Brien
Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@acme.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-24T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-window: canary graduation report and minor follow-ups

All — quick readout from today's window. TL;DR: graduated to 50% per plan, small action items below.

What we did:
- Primed KV cache with 2x directed-seed at +10m (per Carlos ask) — hit-rate improved from 42% -> 74% after the second pass.
- 1% hold extended to 15m as agreed, then 10% (20m), 25% (40m), 50% (30m). No abort criteria were hit.
- Observability: p95 latency rose by ~35ms at 50% but stayed under 200ms; token-service errors were flat. No BGP flaps from BroadCloud.

Attachments: operator_playbook_v1.2.pdf (updated with final timestamps), canary-traffic-matrix-20260823.csv (finalized).

Follow-ups/Action items:
1) Connor — please snapshot the canary route probe config and push to config repo (small delta change).
2) Markus — run a scheduled full priming job overnight to get steady-state KV hit-rate >80%.
3) Acme — if you see any delayed downstream reconciliation (billing events), open HubSpot ticket HUBSPOT-ACME-12458 and tag Maya.

Thanks everyone for the clean window. I'll close the bridge notes and update the shared playbook with the embedded decisions.

— Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai
